new_jobs.description:
Position/Program Information

EXAM NUMBER

AG8194B-R

TYPE OF RECRUITMENT

We welcome applications from anyone.

WHEN TO APPLY

We will be accepting online applications from Wednesday, September 23, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. (PT) until Monday, September 28, 2026, 5:00 PM (PT).

All applications must be received before 5:00 p.m. (PT) on Monday, September 28, 2026, to be accepted.

WHY WORK FOR US?

The Aging and Disabilities Department (AD) serves the growing population of older adults, dependent adults, and individuals with disabilities in Los Angeles County. The department offers a broad range of services aimed at fostering dignity, independence, and overall well-being. Through compassionate and intentional support, AD ensures that individuals can live fulfilling lives within their communities, maintaining the highest quality of life possible. We partner with non-profits, community-based organizations, commissions, and other government agencies to provide services such as social, educational and recreational services, training and education programs, accessibility services, wellness and nutrition programs, emergency preparedness and response programs, home-delivery meal services, in-home visiting programs, crisis intervention, legal services involving fraud, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and other issues that pertain to the older and dependent adults in the community.

Essential Job Functions

Plans, organizes, assigns, and coordinates the work of the organizational unit, resolving policy issues and problems as they arise.
Advises department administration on policy issues involving the work of the organizational unit.
Has responsibility for major administrative functions such as budget, accounting, personnel, or internal support services.
Develops and implements solutions to complex problems of organization, budget, personnel, or procedures that occur within the Program Manager's area of responsibility.
Plans, organizes, and directs the work of subordinate staff in: Development of comprehensive plans and service priorities for Departmental programs; Development of contractor selection and contracting systems; Management of contract monitoring and compliance mechanisms; Working with advisory bodies and the public to elicit the opinions and advice of these interested parties.
Directs Senior and Service Center managers and staff in the delivery of direct services to the public.
Formulates recommendations of departmental policies and procedures.
Maintains liaison with a variety of officials, agencies, and organizations in complex or high level matters concerning the Department.
Coordinates the work of the organizational unit with that of other County departments and divisions.
Represents the department before subcommittees and full meetings of various advisory councils, workshops, conferences, and meetings of special committees.

For more information, please view the classification specification: Program Manager, Workforce Development, Aging and Community Services

Requirements

REQUIREMENTS TO QUALIFY

OPTION 1
One (1) year of experience at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Project Supervisor, Community Services* , or higher, responsible for the development and/or implementation of community development and older adult services or related programs**.

OPTION 2

Three (3) years of experience at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Community Center Director I* ** , or higher, one (1) year of which must include supervision during the last three (3) years, participating in the development and/or implementation of community development and older adult services or related programs** or in departmental administrative support functions.

OPTION 3

Three (3) years of experience in a highly responsible administrative capacity**** analyzing and making recommendations for the solution of problems of organization, financial services, human resources, or information technology, one (1) year of which must have been at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Administrative Services Manager III*****, directing or assisting in directing an administrative, human resources, financial services, or information technology program unit in the service of Los Angeles County.

Special Requirement Information

Project Supervisor, Community Services is defined as having responsibility for supervising a special project involving the development and implementation of service programs that require direct community participation. Qualifying experience at this level must include responsibility for planning, developing, implementing, coordinating, and/or evaluating community-based service programs, rather than solely supervising staff, volunteers, events, or routine program activities.
Community development and older adult services or related programs refers to organized programs designed to address community needs or provide services to older adults and other targeted populations. Such programs may include, but are not limited to, community engagement and outreach, older adult services, social or supportive services, health and wellness programs, educational or recreational programs, resource and referral services, or other programs intended to improve access to services and community well-being.
Community Center Director I is defined as serving as the administrative head of a diversified, multi-service community center or older adult services center.
Highly responsible administrative capacity is defined as administrative work involving substantial responsibility for analyzing, evaluating, developing, and/or recommending solutions to complex organizational, financial services, human resources, or information technology problems, policies, procedures, programs, or operations. Qualifying experience must require the exercise of significant independent judgment, analytical ability, discretion, and responsibility in making recommendations or decisions that affect departmental programs or operations.
*Administrative Services Manager III is defined as directing a section composed of multiple units responsible for providing administrative services that directly impact the management of major departmental programs and operations.

Note:
You may still qualify even if your job title isn’t exactly the same as the ones listed. What matters is that your experience is at a similar level — meaning your job involves similar responsibilities, requires comparable skills and knowledge, and takes place within a similar organizational structure. Please provide a clear explanation of your experience to demonstrate that it is at the appropriate level.

Withhold Information

No withholds will be allowed. Required experience must be fully met and indicated on the application by the last day of filing, and clearly indicated on the application.

Endorsement Of County Qualifications

If you’re a County employee that performed work that differs from the duties described in your class specification and believe you qualify for this opportunity, please provide verification via official documentation of additional responsibility bonus, out-of-class bonus, temporary assignment bonus or reclassification study with CEO Classification within seven (7) calendar days from the last day of filing. Employees do not need to submit such verification if they hold or have held a position that regularly performs functions in alignment with the requirements.

License

A valid California Class C Driver License or the ability to use an alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions.

Physical Class

2 – Light: This class includes administrative and clerical positions requiring light physical effort that may include occasional light lifting to a 10-pound limit and some bending, stooping, or squatting. Considerable ambulation may be involved.

Additional Information

OUR ASSESSMENT PROCESS

Once we have identified that you meet our requirements, an invitation regarding the following assessment process will be sent:

Examination Content

This examination will consist of a multiple-choice and simulation assessment, worth 100% assessing:

Management Judgement
Willingness to Learn
Empathy
Working Relationships
Sharing Knowledge and Guidance
Analyzing Information
Learning Quickly
Generating New Ideas
Using time Efficiently
Working to High Quality Standards
Adapting to Change
Controlling Emotions
Achievement
Responsibility
Management Potential
Deductive Reasoning
Reading Comprehension

Applicants must receive a passing score of 70% or higher on the assessment to be added to the

list.

Exam Review

STANDARDIZED MULTIPLE CHOICE TESTS ARE NOT REVIEWABLE BY CANDIDATES PER CIVIL SERVICE RULE 7.19 .

Transfer of Test Components

If you have taken identical components recently for other exams, your responses may be automatically transferred to this examination. This exam contains test components that might be used on future exams, and your responses could be transferred to that exam.

Test preparation

We provide study guides and other test preparation resources to help candidates prepare for employment tests. While the guides may help in preparing for the test, we recommend reviewing all related materials that seem necessary.

Various information can be found on our website at https://hr.lacounty.gov/job-search-toolkit/ . The section dedicated to test preparation is "Employment Test Assistance."

Eligibility and Vacancy Information

Applicants who passed the assessment are placed on a list for a period of six (6) months. We will use this list to fill vacancies in the Department of Aging and Disabilities as they occur.

Application and Filing information

We only accept applications filed online. Applications submitted by U.S. mail, fax, or in person are not accepted. Apply online by clicking on the "Apply" green button at the top right of this posting. This website can also be used to get application status updates.

About The Job

Community Mental Health Program Manager (ARMHS and DVSA)

Objective/Overview

This position is one of 2 clinical and program leadership positions in Community Mental Health at CUHCC. The Community Mental Health programs include Adult Rehabilitative Mental Health Services (ARMHS), Adult Targeted Case Management (TCM) and Domestic Violence/Sexual Assault (DVSA) programs. This position oversees and directs the practice of ARMHS as well as the DVSA community-based programs.

The State of MN Dept. of Human Services regulations covering ARMHS services allows for 2 roles in the ARMHS program: Clinical Supervisor and Treatment Director. This position combines both of those functions. The position requires licensure as an independent clinician in a mental health field.

Direct reports of: Mental health practitioners, unlicensed and prelicensed, 6.0 FTEs who provide Adult Rehabilitative Mental Health Services (ARMHS) and 2.0 FTEs who provide Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault (DVSA) services.

Essential Functions

Coordinate ARMHS program compliance, quality assurance and clinical supervision, consultation, training and staff development (40%)

Manage ARMHS services to comply with State of MN guidelines and Rule 245i requirements.
Manage staff productivity and access to services to meet program budgetary targets
Act as contact person for State of Minnesota DHS ARMHS regulator and auditing services.
Maintain protocols and procedures for ARMHS services for a multi-cultural patient population within the guidelines of the State of MN ARMHS regulations.
Develop and implement training to meet the needs of mental health practitioner staff.
Explore and implement program and service development.
Facilitate and lead team meetings and provide clinical supervision
Participates in the leadership team at CUHCC focusing on integration of all CUHCC services

Coordinate DVSA program compliance, quality assurance and clinical supervision, consultation, training and staff development (20%)

Ensure compliance with grant requirements, including service delivery as well as grant reporting documents. Collaborate with internal Grants and Contracts management staff to produce reports as needed.
Lead outreach/advocacy/community education efforts with particular populations of focus. These programs are grant-funded, some through State of MN entities, and some are foundation-funded.
Participate in program evaluation and improvement activities
Facilitate and lead team meetings and provide weekly supervision

Staff management: (20%)

Recruit, train and manage performance of ARMHS and DVSA providers in accordance with clinic policies and U of MN Human Resources policies.
Ensure quality of staff documentation of ARMHS interventions and required state documentation
Provide regular supervision to staff, and participate with other Behavioral Health managers in planning staff supervision and consultation to meet various program requirements.
Ensure ARMHS and DVSA staff productivity is at expected levels.

Clinical Services: (20%)

Provide one-on-one, family or group therapy to a caseload of children and/or adults
Complete diagnostic assessments for therapy caseload, in addition to those needing an assessment to enter one or more of CUHCC’s community programs

Qualifications

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

BA/BS and six years professional work experience or advanced degree and four years professional work experience.
Current independent clinician’s license in mental health field, in MN, which is acceptable to CUHCC under the terms of the clinic’s FQHC status. (Includes: LMFT, LICSW, LPCC, MALP or PhDLP, MSCNS or MD).
At least 2 years experience in providing direct patient care to diverse populations.
Excellent communication skills, written and spoken English.
Computer skills: Microsoft Office experience and ability to learn and effectively utilize electronic health record systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Fluency in one of CUHCC’s dominant languages – Spanish, Somali, Pashto, Hmong, or Vietnamese.
At least 2 years experience in program development and quality assurance activities.
At least 2 years experience in staff management.
Experience and/or knowledge of ARMHS services and/or other community programs in mental health

At CUHCC, we're transforming urban health care and educating the next generation of healthcare professionals.

CUHCC offers a full range of dental and mental health services that are typically not offered at a community health center, such as prosthodontic services and psychiatry. CUHCC has pharmacists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, dentists, dental hygienists, nurses, family nurse practitioners, family practice physicians, internal medicine physicians, internal medicine-pediatric physicians, licensed social workers and psychologists among other disciplines on staff.

CUHCC's interprofessional care model uses a collaborative, team-based approach to deliver education and patient care, integrating these services. Students and residents at CUHCC have the opportunity to work with other students and preceptors in other fields to best serve the complex needs of the patients. Over half of CUHCC’s mental health patients also receive medical services at CUHCC, allowing CUHCC providers to work collaboratively to provide patient centered care.

As a founding member in the country's first accountable care organization (ACO) for federally qualified health centers, CUHCC is leading change in urban health and improving patient outcomes to meet the Institute for Healthcare Improvement's Triple Aim: improve the patient experience, improve patient health, and reduce the cost of patient care.

new_jobs.description:
Description

The Design, Sustainability and Engineering team in GREF seeks an experienced Program Manager with strong cross-functional leadership skills to own GREF’s Global Furniture Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E) Program. This role is the single point of strategic ownership for FF&E lifecycle management, procurement strategy, asset management, and cross-functional coordination across GREF's worldwide workplace portfolio.

The FF&E function within GREF covers four primary responsibilities: defining and maintaining FF&E standards and strategy, stewarding the Workplace FF&E Standards, driving regional procurement strategies, sustainability, and benchmarking against industry practice to identify gaps and improvements.

This role serves as the connective tissue between Global Design, Workplace Guidelines, Construction delivery teams, GREF Finance, Global Corporate Sustainability, Portfolio Management, and Global Corporate Procurement (GCP). The successful candidate will integrate constraints and requirements from cross-functional stakeholders into efficient, scalable, globally-relevant solutions that are fiscally responsible and advance Amazon's sustainability commitments.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end FF&E Lifecycle Management Strategy across GREF's global portfolio — from specification and procurement through operations, storage, and end-of-life disposition.
Own and drive the FF&E procurement strategy, partnering with GCP under the shared-accountability model to co-own joint savings commitments while balancing regional availability, sustainability, and cost caps
Own global FF&E Asset Tracking (AST) strategy across all GREF-supported sites, including asset storage, product ordering, inventory management, and evaluation of aging products to meet requirements of 100% inventory coverage and >90% data quality accuracy. Develop and enforce governance, risk and compliance controals for FF&E including monthly verification tracking, sadhbaords scopes and compliance evidence documentation
Establish and maintain furniture asset lifetime guidelines, condition assessment criteria, and refurbishment standards that inform replacement planning, budget forecasting, and warranty alignment
Collaborate in develop and manage a global FF&E circularity program — identifying, cataloging, and redistributing surplus assets to avoid unnecessary new purchases; establish partnerships with internal reuse functions, donation, resale, takeback programs and recycling partners for end-of-life disposition
Own the GREF Workplace FF&E Standards (selection, testing, digital catalog) and FF&E Guidelines (design guidance, trade up/down decision logic, playbooks for internal and external teams)
Develop the FF&E technology strategy, inclusive of disposal method tracking, including evaluating and driving decisions on platform capabilities, integration architecture across regional systems, and AI-enabled asset discovery tools
Benchmark industry best practices, identify gaps between Global Workplace Design Guidelines and regional trends, and provide solution-oriented recommendations
Lead cross-functional stakeholder alignment across Design, Construction, MAC, Portfolio Management, Procurement, Finance, IT, AV, Security, and sustainability teams
Develop cost-avoidance tracking and reporting to quantify savings from procurement consolidation, reuse programs, and vendor strategy; coordinate environmental impact reporting (waste diversion, embodied carbon reduction)

A day in the life

This role is deeply cross-functional. You'll partner daily with Design, Construction, Procurement, Finance, Sustainability, Portfolio Management, and regional operations teams — aligning competing priorities into one global strategy for how Amazon's furniture is specified, procured, tracked, reused, and retired. One conversation might be negotiating a global seating contract; the next, advancing a circular economy partnership or troubleshooting asset data quality with a regional lead across the world. You own the system end-to-end, and you'll measure impact in millions saved and tons diverted from landfill.

About The Team

The Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) team manages Amazon's real estate and facilities globally. It's organized into Regional Portfolio Management, Global Centers of Enablement, and Global Centers of Expertise. Design, Sustainability and Engineering includes Global Design, Workplace Guidelines, Sustainability, and Engineering teams. These teams develop design concepts, implement workplace standards, and deliver various spaces across Amazon's portfolio. GREF emphasizes inclusive team culture, work-life balance, and career growth. The team values diversity and promotes knowledge sharing and mentorship. GREF strives to create spaces that support Amazonians' work while enhancing employee well-being and aligning with the company's strategic vision.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree
Knowledge of financial asset classification including capitalization thresholds and Special Economic Zone compliance implications for asset registries
Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions
BA/BS in Business, Supply Chain, Facilities Management, Architecture, Interior Design, or related field

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Ryan Companies US, Inc. has an exciting career opportunity for a Commissioning Program Manager to join our National Mission Critical team!

The Commissioning Program Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating the commissioning program across multiple construction projects for a single client. This role establishes and maintains commissioning standards, oversees project execution, and supports field teams to ensure building systems are planned, installed, tested, and documented in accordance with performance, quality, and safety requirements. The Commissioning Program Manager serves as a key liaison between internal stakeholders, design teams, subcontractors, and owners to drive successful handover of high-performing facilities.

Some Things You Can Expect To Do

Program Leadership & Strategy

Develop and maintain company-wide commissioning procedures, standards, and best practices.
Manage commissioning project delivery strategies across all applicable project sites.
Develop, implement, and ensure project participation in the company commissioning program and processes.
Refine commissioning practices and policies used in the field and develop methods/techniques for driving issues to resolution.
Regularly review commissioning progress, risks, issues, and KPI metrics across active projects and report to management.
Support hiring efforts for commissioning managers and personnel as needed.
Assist in staffing and resource allocation planning for commissioning across multiple projects.

Team Leadership & Guidance

Lead, mentor, and performance-manage a team of commissioning professionals.
Provide training and guidance to field teams on commissioning sequencing, durations, and expectations.
Coordinate and, when needed, lead commissioning kickoff meetings to describe commissioning objectives and requirements to equipment vendors, subcontractors, and owner representatives.
Promote a culture of safety, quality, and accountability within the commissioning team.
Role should expect to have up to 8 direct reports.

Project Coordination & Support

Review design documents to understand and communicate system performance requirements for each project.
Ensure project commissioning teams are aware of and aligned with design intent and performance criteria.
Attend key owner/architect/contractor (OAC), commissioning, and coordination meetings as required.
Manage high-level coordination and issue resolution with clients, vendors, and other stakeholders when critical commissioning issues arise.
Provide project teams with guidance on commissioning schedule integration, issue tracking and closure, client communications, and general commissioning management.

Field Oversight & Execution

Ensure field inspections, functional testing, and documentation support the successful execution of the quality and commissioning program.
Collaborate with project teams to monitor progress of commissioning activities and ensure alignment with project milestones.
Provide on-site support at active projects as required to troubleshoot issues and support successful commissioning execution.

Continuous Improvement & Knowledge Sharing

Implement and maintain commissioning KPIs and continuous improvement processes to prevent repeat deficiencies and minimize impacts to project schedules.
Capture, document, and communicate lessons learned across projects to improve future commissioning efforts.
Contribute to the development of training materials, tools, and templates that support consistent commissioning delivery.

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, building systems, or related field; or equivalent experience.
10+ years of experience in commercial construction, MEP systems, or related technical field including 5+ years of experience in data center commissioning; multi-project or program-level experience preferred.
Strong understanding of building systems (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, and life safety).
Proven experience leading commissioning activities on complex or large-scale projects.
Experience coordinating with owners, design teams, contractors, and vendors in a construction environment.

You Will Really Stand Out If You

Have earned professional certifications related to commissioning, building systems, or project management (e.g., CxA, CEM, PE, PMP).

new_jobs.title: ITC/PTC Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About The Company

Founded in 2010, Eagle Creek Renewable Energy (ECRE) acquires, enhances, and operates hydroelectric power facilities across the United States. Today, Eagle Creek owns and operates 85 facilities across 18 states, with a nearly 700 MW portfolio that provides reliable, low-carbon power to more than 260,000 homes.

Eagle Creek is committed to creating long-term value for its stakeholders and the communities it serves through a focus on safety, integrity, innovation, diversity, and stewardship. Through strategic investments, operational excellence, and continued growth, the company aims to expand its renewable energy platform and play a meaningful role in the transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future.

Summary of the Position

ECRE is seeking a versatile, self-directed, and highly organized ITC/PTC Program Manager
to drive the end-to-end lifecycle of our Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and Production Tax Credit (PTC) initiatives for our hydropower portfolio. In this role, you will serve as the single point of accountability, bridging cross-functional inputs, and owning the qualification work and the evidence set that makes each facility’s credits defensible.

While you will not be expected to be a tax code expert or a lead design engineer, you must possess enough technical fluency to understand hydropower project lifecycles, track vendor deliverables, interpret high-level IRS compliance requirements, and manage cross-functional timelines and budgets.

Main Responsibilities

Credit Qualification Oversight: Serve as the single point of coordination for tracking and verifying all inputs, documentation, and milestones required to secure ITC/PTC qualifications
Audit & Diligence Readiness: Maintain a clean, contemporaneous qualification file for each facility that withstands tax-preparer, credit-buyer, insurer, and IRS review
Cross-Functional Coordination: Act as the central hub for a matrixed team, aligning inputs from supporting departments to support qualification requirements
IRS Compliance Alignment: Work alongside internal tax specialists to interpret high-level IRS requirements and ensure that project workflows capture the necessary evidentiary trail for tax compliance
Vendor & Deliverable Tracking: Monitor external vendor and contractor deliverables specifically tied to tax credit qualification requirements, ensuring reports, studies, and certifications are delivered on schedule
Schedule & Milestone Monitoring: Maintain a master program tracker to monitor critical path qualification milestones, ensuring that project execution timelines managed by the PM team align with tax deadlines and safe-harbor rules
Executive Reporting: Prepare clear, concise executive-level dashboards and status reports summarizing program health, qualification risks, and key decision points for leadership and ownership

Education & Experience Requirements

Required:

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Project Management, Business, or a related technical/analytical field
Experience: 3 to 8+ years of professional experience in energy project development, asset management, project controls, or renewable energy finance/tax credit compliance. Hydropower experience is a strong plus
Cross-Functional Fluency: Basic familiarity with energy tax credits (ITC/PTC) and an eagerness to learn IRS regulatory frameworks with the support of internal specialists
Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered where appropriate

Competencies

The successful candidate should demonstrate the following competencies:

Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex technical and financial tracking into executive-ready reporting

new_jobs.title: Health and Wellness Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
Are you a person of compassion? An advocate for justice? Someone who stands up for the rights of the vulnerable and speaks out for the marginalized, the exploited and the forgotten?  Do you believe in our calling as Christians to welcome the least of these and love our neighbor?

If you answered ‘yes’, to any of the above, World Relief, and millions of people around the world need you.

At this pivotal moment in time, we are rapidly expanding and growing our team to meet the increasing needs of our world. We are looking for people who want to use their gifts and talents to make a real and tangible difference in our world and the lives of the suffering.

If you’re looking for a purpose-driven career in which you can grow your talents, while also standing up for the rights of the vulnerable, we want you to join us today.

ORGANIZATION SUMMARY

World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. The organization was founded in the aftermath of World War II to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of war-torn Europe. Since then, for 80 years, across 100 countries, World Relief has partnered with local churches and communities to build a world where families thrive and communities flourish.

Today, organizational programming focuses on humanitarian and disaster response, community strengthening and resilience, and refugee & immigrant services and advocacy.

POSITION SUMMARY:

World Relief seeks a Health and Wellness Case Manager to support vulnerable immigrants in building pathways to physical, emotional, and social well-being. This position provides Intensive Case Management (ICM) for individuals and families, alongside wellness-focused group programming that promotes health education and community integration. Working in a dual-capacity role, the Case Manager guides clients through complex healthcare systems, crafts tailored goal plans for long-term stability and collaborates with health providers and community partners to deliver trauma-informed, fully compliant care.

This is a hybrid role- 4 days in office, 1 work from home.

ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Client Services and Role Responsibilities

PC Groups & Intensive Case Management

Oversee all incoming Preferred Communities (PC) referrals, conducting comprehensive intake assessments and client enrollments.

Provide direct Intensive Case Management (ICM) to develop and implement targeted, individualized goal plans that foster long-term self-sufficiency.

Maintain regular, proactive communication with clients throughout their service term to monitor progress, address emerging needs, and provide continuous support.

Guide clients through healthcare, social service, and community systems to build their independence and confidence.

Maintain precise, timely documentation and detailed case notes in full alignment with program standards and compliance guidelines

Interdepartmental Collaboration & Wrap-Around Care

Work closely with the Programs Manager and program staff to streamline client service delivery across department lines.

Partner with the Volunteer Coordinator to engage, train, and leverage volunteers or community groups for integrated client support.

Deliver holistic, wrap-around care by connecting clients to wrap-around community services and advocacy networks.

Compliance, Data Management & Quality Assurance:

Assure all compliance measures are strictly maintained across all PC programming and service delivery.

Ensure data collection and outcome tracking are conducted in a timely, accurate, and effective manner for reporting and evaluation.

Administrative Responsibilities

Actively participate in department meetings, staff development opportunities, program trainings, community activities, and organizational events

Submit any requested data to the program manager through monthly, semi-annual, and annual reports.

Maintain accurate and organized files and records of services provided

Ensure continuity of services and reporting during staff transitions and in the absence of a Programs Manager

Adhere to all World Relief policies, including but not limited to, incident reporting procedures, code of conduct, security safety and health

Travel to and between High Point and Winston Salem office locations is a requirement for this position

Perform other tasks and projects as assigned

Note: This job description outlines the primary responsibilities of the role but is not exhaustive; the Case Manager may be assigned additional tasks or duties by the Programs Manager as needed

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

Mature and personal Christian faith  

Committed to the mission, vision, and values of World Relief  

Desire to serve and empower the Church to impact vulnerable communities  

Able to affirm World Relief’s Core Beliefs and Statement of Faith , and acknowledge World  

Relief’s Christian Identity and National Evangelicals For the Health of The Nation document    

Valid driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle and ability to pass MVR standards 

Experience in case management, health education, or related fields required; experience with refugee or vulnerable populations preferred.   

Highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple cases simultaneously and prioritize tasks effectively.  

Strong understanding of the challenges faced by refugees and immigrants, including trauma-informed care and cultural sensitivity.  

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey information to clients, colleagues, and external partners.  

Strong interpersonal skills, including empathy, active listening, and conflict resolution.  

Fluency in English required. Bilingual in any of the following languages: Arabic, Swahili, Spanish, French, Kareni, Burmese, Pashto, Dari

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Degree in Social Work, Public Health, or similar field.

Cross-cultural experience.

Bilingual in any of the following languages: Arabic, Swahili, Spanish, French, Kareni, Burmese, Pashto, Dari

St. Patrick Center provides opportunities for self-sufficiency and dignity to people who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless. Individuals and families build permanent, positive change in their lives through safe and affordable housing, sound mental and physical health, and employment and financial stability.

Working collaboratively with individuals, businesses, government and other service providers, St. Patrick Center will end chronic homelessness in the St. Louis region through Housing First, an evidence-based practice that tells us to remove barriers, do intake and assessment early, move people into housing and offer them support to achieve their goals.

Job Summary

Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of St. Louis, St. Patrick Center, is seeking a Case Manager to join the Housing, Employment and Recovery Opportunities (HERO) program. This individual will utilize wrap-around philosophy and techniques to assist clients in transitional housing. The case manager will meet with clients to maintain family and natural supports in the community, collaborate with clients and track the success of the Individual Service Strategy (ISS)/Treatment Plan of Care, coordinate individualized services and the involvement of providers working in the home and community setting and document all support related to activities and services. The core working hours are 8:00am-4:30pm Monday through Friday. This position is located at Freedom Place, an offsite location. Starting Compensation is $45,000.

Visit clients weekly to track ISS goals.
Transport clients to community partner appointments
Contribute to the ideas and processes of the case management team.
Use a peer-to-peer approach to build rapport with individuals in recovery.
Provide emotional and informational support for permanent housing by assessing strengths, desires and immediate and long-term needs of each client.
Develop or contact family and natural supports which exist in the community.
Receive input from case management team members regarding employment, housing, mentoring, substance use, other immediate/long term needs, and long-term financial stability needs.
Complete daily and monthly departmental paperwork
Daily update of electronic files including contact with clients, services or any internal or external referrals made.
Adhere to the strategies and goals outlined in the ISS and Treatment Plan
Coach clients to make solid well-informed decisions which maintain housing and advocate for the client.
Assist client with monthly budgeting.
Complete treatment plans and track goals monthly
Provide financial and money management counseling sessions.
Provide weekly case management sessions to ensure service delivery.
Teach Life Skills classes.
Refer client to additional resources to address other service needs (i.e., legal assistance, VA benefits, community substance use counseling etc.)
Research additional benefits available to enhance service being provided.
Engage the client, the family and natural supports within the community setting when feasible and desired by client.
Networks with federal, state, and local agencies
Any other duties as assigned.

Knowledge of housing and other supportive service resources.
Knowledge of Housing First and Harm Reduction.

The Community Health Worker focuses on direct support, outreach, and engagement to improve community health outcomes, focusing on improving health, well-being, and access to essential services. Maintains accurate and up-to-date records to support advocacy efforts, monitor outcomes, and contribute to program evaluation.

The Corporate Office of Express Employment International is seeking a dynamic VMS Project Specialist to join our VMS MSP Team. In this impactful role, you will drive strategic sales and account development initiatives while playing a key part in managing VMS client programs. Acting as a trusted operational partner, you will combine data-driven insights, proactive client and MSP support, and continuous process optimization to enhance program performance and deliver exceptional client experiences.

This position can be considered remote. However, Express Employment International believes in the value of in-person collaboration to support teamwork, creativity and connection. Employees in this position who are located within the Oklahoma City metropolitan market are expected to work a four (4) day in-office schedule, with the flexibility to work remotely one (1) day each week, based on business and department needs.

Responsibilities

Maintain deep expertise in the financial and operational requirements of all VMS accounts managed by Program Managers, serving as a reliable backup and trusted advisor. Act as a direct point of contact for clients, offices, and MSP partners, making timely business decisions to ensure seamless program delivery
Demonstrate strong proficiency in the day-to-day operations of Vendor Management System (VMS) tools and platforms, ensuring accurate and efficient program management
Analyze operational and financial reports to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, delivering actionable insights that drive informed decision-making and program optimization
Play a key role in new client implementations by leading critical activities such as coordinating background packages from approved vendors, building worker uploads, provisioning VMS access for offices, developing client-specific tools, and creating onboarding materials. Serve as a vital contributor during VMS transitions for existing clients
Support the Strategic Sales team throughout the sales cycle by actively participating in prospect calls, internal strategy sessions, and other initiatives as needed
Continuously evaluate and optimize existing processes to increase sales performance, enhance operational efficiency, and improve the overall experience for franchisees, office staff, clients, and MSP partners. Proactively deliver recommendations to the Director and Program Managers to drive meaningful improvements
Leverage and maximize a variety of technology platforms — including advanced VMS systems, Microsoft Teams, and the full Microsoft Office suite — to boost productivity and deliver exceptional results

Education & Experience Qualifications

1-3 years of hands-on experience in a Vendor Management System or Managed Service Provider role, such as VMS Coordinator or VMS Specialist
Four-year degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills, Or Abilities

Self-motivated and proactive, with the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment while effectively managing multiple tasks and maintaining high productivity with minimal supervision
Strong decision-making and judgment skills, capable of drawing on experience and company guidelines to make timely, effective decisions and communicate confidently with stakeholders at all levels
Excellent time management and prioritization abilities, with a high sense of urgency and the capacity to differentiate between urgent and important tasks to consistently meet deadlines

Not sure you meet every requirement? Apply anyway!

At Express, we celebrate what makes you, you. We value diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and talents—because we know that’s what makes us stronger together. If you're excited about the role, we’re excited to hear from you.

Express Employment International supports Express Employment Professionals franchises and related brands. The Express franchise brand is an industry-leading, international staffing company with more than 870 franchise locations in the U.S., Canada, South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand.

new_jobs.title: Enterprise Strategic Planning Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Posting closes at 11:59 PM the day before the listed end date.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite in Richland, WA.

General Summary

The Strategic Planning Program Manager leads Energy Northwest's Strategic Planning Program and strategic performance reporting processes. The position is responsible for maintaining the agency's strategic planning framework, supporting development and communication of strategic priorities, monitoring organizational performance against strategic objectives, and facilitating alignment between agency leadership, member utilities, and enterprise planning activities.

Working closely with executive leadership, department leaders, Public Affairs, Board Relations, and member utilities, the position helps ensure Energy Northwest maintains a clear understanding of its strategic priorities, progress toward objectives, and long-term direction as a public power Joint Operating Agency. The position supports long-range planning that balances stewardship of the agency's existing enterprise with development of future capabilities, resources, and services that position Energy Northwest to meet the evolving needs of member utilities.

Principal Accountabilities

Strategic Planning

Lead development, administration, and continuous improvement of Energy Northwest's Strategic Planning Program, strategic goals, measures, and planning priorities.
Coordinate strategic planning activities involving executive leadership, departments, member utilities, the Executive Board, and the Board of Directors.
Coordinate long-range strategic planning activities that support the agency's existing enterprise while positioning Energy Northwest for future strategic opportunities.
Develop and administer processes for gathering strategic planning input from member utilities and other stakeholders.
Monitor industry, policy, regulatory, market, and public power trends that may impact the agency's long-term strategy.

Performance Reporting

Lead development and administration of strategic performance reporting and monitoring processes.
Develop, maintain, and communicate strategic scorecards, balanced scorecards, performance measures, and related planning metrics.
Analyze and communicate organizational progress toward strategic objectives and priorities.
Coordinate action planning and follow-up activities associated with strategic performance measures.

Communications & Alignment

Develop strategic planning content, presentations, briefing materials, reports, and planning updates.
Partner with Public Affairs, Finance, Enterprise Risk, and Operations to support communication and engagement activities related to agency strategy.
Promote shared understanding of strategic priorities across the organization and among member utilities.
Coordinate integration between strategic goals, business planning, performance measures, and agency priorities to support execution of the agency’s strategic plan.
Promote alignment between strategic priorities, business planning, and organizational performance to support execution of the agency's long-term strategy.

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration or related field and seven years of experience in strategic planning, business planning, utility operations, organizational performance, public affairs, or related field;

OR
Associate’s degree in Business Administration or a related field and nine years of experience in strategic planning, business planning, utility operations, organizational performance, public affairs, or related field;

OR
High School diploma/GED and eleven years of experience in strategic planning, business planning, utility operations, organizational performance, public affairs, or related field.

Desired Education And Experience

Experience in public power, Joint Operating Agency, cooperative or utility; enterprise strategic planning; board support; regional energy policy/resource planning, executive support and cross-functional coordination.

Pay Range

$126,362.00 - $157,952.00 Annual

The salary listed represents the pay range for this position. Starting pay is calculated from the minimum of the salary range and actual individual placement within the range is determined based on the candidate's experience, education, skills, and abilities related to the role. The level and final offer will also take into account the candidate's overall qualifications.

Incentive Compensation

This position is eligible for an annual at-risk compensation (ARC) incentive plan. Incentives are earned based on agency performance against defined metrics and goals which follow eligibility rules within the ARC plan document.

Benefits

Energy Northwest (EN) provides a phenomenal benefits package. Washington State also has no state income tax, and the Tri-Cities provides a cost-of-living lower than the national average.

EN offers substantial retirement benefits through three retirement programs including the Washington State Public Employees' Retirement System pension plan (PERS), a 401(k) savings plan with an employer match component, and a 457(b) savings plan. EN also offers multiple options for medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance coverage. Other voluntary benefits may include flexible spending accounts (FSAs), tuition reimbursement, student loan repayment, childcare subsides, health reimbursement arrangement (HRA VEBA), health savings account (HSA), supplemental life insurances, credit monitoring/identity theft insurance, and more! Qualifying employees will typically start a personal time accrual rate of 160 hours per year and EN provides nine paid holidays throughout the Calander year; personal time accruals grow significantly at various service intervals.
